title: Imaging Mass Cytometry Compensation Slide Preparation
author: Michelle Daniel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf2djqa6
materials: Let the slide dry for at least 1h.

steps.title: Prepare agarose‑coated slide
steps.instruction: Coat a microscopy slide with a thin, homogeneous layer of 2 % agarose and let it dry.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 2 % agarose solution in ddH₂O in a small beaker and melt it (e.g., in a microwave).
Preheat the microscopy slide to 70 °C on a hot plate.
Dispense approximately 350–400 µL of the liquid agarose onto the slide until the surface is fully covered.
Allow the agarose layer to dry for at least 30 minutes; the coat should become very thin, homogeneous, and barely visible.
Store the dried agarose‑coated slides at room temperature in dry conditions until further use.

steps.title: Create metal spots on slide
steps.instruction: Deposit trypan‑blue spots and add antibody‑conjugates to generate metal spots for compensation.

substeps.instruction: Pipette an array of 0.3 µL trypan‑blue spots onto the agarose‑coated slide, keeping spots well separated; make one spot for each antibody‑conjugated mass channel used in the study.
In AirLab, open the relevant antibody panel and print it out for reference.
Retrieve all listed antibody conjugates from the 4 °C refrigerator and keep them on ice.

For each antibody conjugate, pipette 0.2 µL onto the corresponding trypan‑blue spot on the slide. Record the exact location of each conjugate and ensure no material bleeds over; optionally sort the antibodies by the mass of their conjugated metal.
Let the slide dry for at least 1 hour.
Store the slide at room temperature in a dedicated box until measurement.
